summary: The generated Playwright tests are functionally sound with proper asynchronous handling, correct use of API, and valid TypeScript syntax. Each test case includes the testCaseId in the title and correctly maps to the intended test steps. Assertions target locators properly and use 'await' where required. Some selector usage relies on roles and labels which may become brittle if the UI changes; also, hardcoded expected options in test TC-003 might lead to fragility if the dropdown items change. Overall, the tests are maintainable and reusable, but selector robustness and externalizing test data could be improved.

issues.description: Selectors rely on roles and labels which may be fragile if UI or accessibility roles change.
issues.recommendation: Consider using more robust data-testid attributes or stable element identifiers for selectors.

issues.description: Test data such as expected dropdown options and input message strings are hardcoded inside tests.
issues.recommendation: Externalize test data into data files or test fixtures to improve maintainability and reuse.

recommendations: Enhance selector resilience by using dedicated test attributes where possible.
Extract test data into separate files or constants for better maintenance.
Add validation on navigation to confirm landing on the correct page before interacting with elements.
Consider wrapping repetitive navigation steps into reusable test hooks or functions.
